description: Repairs r-ado-1b/txn-client-cache-rollback: the keyset and the client optimistic recordset both wrote ID 2, so which route wrote the surviving "txr-2" was not traced. Each route now writes its own row. On a read-write copy of r-ado-1b-main: a server keyset optimistic, a server static read-only, a client static optimistic and a client static batch-optimistic recordset of SELECT ID, S FROM T ORDER BY ID are opened; BeginTrans; the Connection UPDATEs S of ID 1 to "txc-cn"; the keyset recordset edits and Updates S of ID 2 to "txr-keyset"; the client optimistic one edits and Updates S of ID 3 to "txr-client"; the batch one edits S of ID 4 to "txr-batch" and calls UpdateBatch; Connection.Errors read and cleared. Each recordset reads ID and S of every row and RecordCount; RollbackTrans; each reads the same again without refresh, then after Resync(adAffectAll, adResyncAllValues), then after Requery; the stored rows through Execute and through a DAO read-only snapshot. Asks what each cursor's cache shows after the rollback, which route's change survives and which refresh restores the stored values.
retentionNote: Designed r-fix-wire-ado probe (A-02); complete capture of the ACE answer.
